candidates: When writing regex patterns to detect CLI tool or package names in command strings (e.g., in `getCliIntegrationFromAncestry`), never make inter-word separators optional. Use `create[\s\-]rsbuild` rather than `create[\s\-]?rsbuild`; making the separator optional silently matches concatenated forms like `creatersbuild`.

Avoid `.includes()` to detect package or tool names within command strings; it produces false positives when the name appears in a URL, file path, or install argument. Use a regex with position assertions instead — e.g., `/(?:^|\s)@tanstack\/start(?=\s|@|$)/i` — so the match is anchored to an actual invocation context.

When testing CLI integration detection logic (e.g., `getCliIntegrationFromAncestry`), always include: (a) negative cases that confirm unseparated or concatenated variants of the tool name are NOT matched (e.g., `creatersbuild` when only `create-rsbuild` should match), and (b) false-positive edge cases where the target string appears inside a URL, file path, or `npm install` argument to verify the detection pattern is not over-broad.
